mission.title: Our Mission
mission.description: SolarMatch aims to democratize solar feasibility analysis for Egyptian homeowners and businesses. We believe that accurate information is the first step toward sustainable energy adoption, and we're committed to making that information accessible to everyone.

background.title: Project Background
background.p1: SolarMatch was developed as a professional demonstration for a student innovation competition focused on sustainable technology solutions for the Egyptian market.
background.p2: Egypt has exceptional solar potential, with average daily irradiance exceeding 5.5 kWh/m² across most of the country. However, many property owners lack access to reliable tools for evaluating whether solar makes sense for their specific situation.
background.p3: Our platform bridges this gap by combining real NASA climate data with Egypt's actual electricity tariff structure to provide engineering-grade feasibility assessments that anyone can understand.

accuracy.title: Scientific Accuracy
accuracy.description: We use peer-reviewed methodologies and authoritative data sources to ensure our calculations reflect real-world performance

accessibility.title: Accessibility

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about solar energy in Egypt

howMuchCost.q: How much does a solar panel system cost in Egypt?
howMuchCost.a: Solar system costs in Egypt range from 15,000 to 26,000 EGP per kW depending on panel quality. A typical 5kW residential system costs between 75,000-130,000 EGP. Our calculator provides accurate estimates based on your specific requirements and chosen package tier.

roofSize.q: What roof size do I need for solar panels?
roofSize.a: You need approximately 6-8.5 m² per kW of solar capacity, depending on panel efficiency. For a typical 5kW system, you'd need 30-43 m² of usable roof space. Our tool calculates usable area based on your building type (50-75% of total roof).

paybackPeriod.q: How long until the system pays for itself?
paybackPeriod.a: Most residential solar systems in Egypt pay back within 4-7 years, depending on your electricity consumption and local rates. With Egypt's 7-tier tariff system, higher consumers see faster payback. After payback, you enjoy 15-20+ years of free electricity.

maintenance.q: What maintenance do solar panels require?
maintenance.a: Solar panels require minimal maintenance. Regular cleaning every 2-4 weeks during dusty seasons (especially Khamaseen in spring) and monthly during normal periods. No moving parts means very low maintenance costs—typically 1-2% of system cost annually.

gridConnection.q: Do I need to stay connected to the grid?
gridConnection.a: It depends on your coverage ratio. Systems under 100% coverage should stay grid-connected. 100-120% coverage works well with hybrid (grid + battery) systems. Over 120% coverage may allow off-grid operation, though grid connection enables net metering benefits.

lifespan.q: How long do solar panels last?
lifespan.a: Quality solar panels last 25-30 years with minimal degradation (about 0.5% efficiency loss per year). Most manufacturers offer 25-year performance warranties. Inverters typically need replacement after 10-15 years.

weather.q: Do solar panels work in hot weather or cloudy days?
weather.a: Solar panels work year-round but output varies. Egypt's average 5.5+ kWh/m²/day irradiance is excellent. Panels lose about 0.4% efficiency per degree above 25°C. Cloudy days reduce output by 10-25% but still generate power. Our Smart Insights show monthly variations.

permits.q: Do I need permits for solar installation in Egypt?
permits.a: Residential systems under 500 kW typically require notification to the electricity distribution company. Net metering agreements need approval from the local electricity authority. Commercial installations may need additional environmental permits.
